data.note: long-running feature request for LSP client support; closed won't-do in favor of external micro-plugin-lsp
long thread tracking effort to get micro packaged for apt/Debian; eventually succeeded, micro entered official Debian repos and Ubuntu 20.04

long thread on autocompletion; core added simple buffer-word autocomplete natively (2019) plus command/filename completion, but full language-aware autocomplete deferred to LSP plugins (see lsp-support)
long debate on adding a file-tree/sidebar to core; community leaned toward keeping micro a lean editor (not IDE) and resolved via plugins (filetree-plugin, filemanager)
long-running copy/paste confusion thread; explains micro's clipboard model (internal/terminal/external, xclip/xsel dependency, ssh limitations), later improved with OSC52 terminal clipboard support

long-running (2024-2026) architectural rewrite of the highlighter's parsing approach for perf; exponential-time regions bug found, byte-vs-rune line storage tension spun off to #3149, converted back to draft 2025-04-26 for being too hard to follow; both PR authors became maintainers mid-thread

merged: added indenttabchar/indentspacechar/spacechar, deprecating indentchar; design debate over naming vs repurposing indentchar, tabsize-relative highlighting confusion, and whether indent chars should respect tabstospaces (dropped that check); author flagged a follow-up PR adding eol/inv/wrap char options
Go autocomplete via gocode PR, 2018-2021, abandoned; concludes LSP would be better approach
long-running tcell mouse-mode bug: split/garbled SSH escape sequences leak into buffer/terminal, multiple partial fixes over 2017-2020, many duplicate issues cross-referenced
long-standing (2018-2026) high-engagement request to streamline find/find-next: users repeatedly confused that Ctrl-N/Ctrl-G require pressing Enter first after Ctrl-F
SSH clipboard config confusion: terminal/external modes, mouse setting interactions, X11 forwarding workarounds

original multi-cursor feature request/implementation (2016-2017): landed as vim-multiple-cursors-style (Alt-n/p/c/x), not sublime/vscode word-expand-then-ctrl-d style; known bugs at merge time (cursor sync on backspace, cursor merging)
softwrap alone breaks mid-word; users must combine wordwrap+softwrap, a long-undiscovered setting pairing
long-running (2016-2026, 62 thumbs-up) 'show invisibles' request; eventually resolved by indentchar and the showchars option landed in #3760

adds runtime/syntax/default.yaml as filetype:unknown fallback (mail/URL rules only, kept minimal per reviewer pushback on config-file-specific rules); refactors UpdateRules() into findRuntimeSyntaxDef/findRealRuntimeSyntaxDef helpers
merged PR making save() atomic: temp-file+rename with overwrite fallback, symlink resolution, backup reuse, rejects FIFOs/device files/irregular files

maintainer deep-dive (JoeKar+dmaluka) reworking 'reload'/'set filetype'/autosave: reload must skip volatile settings, autosave rearchitected to persistent goroutine w/ retime channel (fixed goroutine leak), filetype-triggered reinit caused duplicate errors/crashes; broke plugins that write buf.Settings directly instead of SetOptionNative

recurring tcell 'terminal entry not found' across TERM values (screen, kitty, cygwin, st); resolved by auto-generating db from infocmp via mkinfo, later built into micro directly, but edge cases persist

PR adding multi-line signature/header-based filetype detection (detectlimit option, filename-check precedence over header regex, tie-break among ambiguous matches by scanning body for a signature); rejected folding detectindent plugin into this same pass (kept as separate plugin, not core)
single-maintainer bottleneck (zyedidia) resolved 2024-03: JoeKar+dmaluka added as maintainers with merge rights; core deps migrated to micro-editor org, main repo migration still pending

long paths overflow backup/serialized-buffer filenames; explored base64/deflate/LUT-of-hashes before settling on: keep URL-encoding as happy path, but when escaped path+suffix exceeds 255 chars, fall back to md5(path) as filename plus a sibling {hash}.path file holding the original path (DetermineEscapePath returns (name, resolveName)); a late review found the fallback path was written outside the backup dir (missing filepath.Join) before merge
owner declined built-in vi/modal mode 2016 (closed, 'rather just use Vim'); recurring feature request since, workarounds are keybinding tweaks or third-party Lua plugins (micro-vi-plugin), never core

FindNext/ReplaceRegex matched ^/$/\b against the search *range* boundaries, not real line start/end, causing false matches mid-line; fixed by padding the regex with a required leading/trailing '.' (non-capturing group) only on the first/last line of the range, then trimming that padding rune back out of the match; settled on compiling the padded variant lazily per line rather than precompiling all 4 combinations; ReplaceRegex needed the same fix via a new findAll() helper, replacing per-line ReplaceAllFunc with per-match deltas processed in reverse
WSL-specific clipboard failures; clip.exe/xclip shims, OSC52 support added, 'set clipboard terminal' workaround, same config-mode confusion as SSH cases

adds overwrite-mode indicator to statusline; state moved to Buffer (not BufPane/Cursor) matching the LastSearch/HighlightSearch precedent so it works correctly per-bufpane even when sharing a buffer; long bikeshed over indicator text (ins/ovr/ovwr/overwrite) settled on fixed-width [ovwr] to avoid statusline resize flicker; made mutually exclusive with [ro] since overwrite is meaningless on a readonly buffer

long-running open issue: micro hangs blank on startup, root-caused to wl-clipboard hanging when reading/writing an empty clipboard (upstream wl-clipboard bug, dup of #2577/#3078/#4079); workarounds are settings.json clipboard:terminal or clipboard:internal, or switching to wl-clipboard-rs

long-running open issue: holding an arrow key to scroll keeps scrolling for seconds after release, on weak/ARM hardware and after macOS window resize; tracked as a 'major' issue via #2970, root causes not fixed but two known CPU hotspots identified during scroll redraws: tcell's CanDisplay() (#3227) and repeated buf.Settings map lookups (#3228); one report traces it to TERM=vt100 vs xterm

PR #3618 (merged): plugins can no longer write settings.json/bindings.json directly (TryBindKeyPlug/SetGlobalOptionPlug set values without persisting to file); new lockbindings option (default false) lets users block plugins from binding keys at all, to guard against accidental irreversible actions from unreviewed keybinds.

maintainer dmaluka pushes back on masmu's SubWord PR: renames IsNonAlphaNumeric->IsNonWordChar, proposes IsSubwordDelimiter, debates WordRight/Left inconsistency vs SubWord; merged 2024-05-21, follow-up trailing-whitespace bug spun into #3321

matchbracestyle enum (underline/highlight) chosen over a boolean for future generic option-toggling (#2086); usability bug found+fixed where reverse-color highlight collided with cursor rendering; design simplified to only match braces the cursor sits directly on, dropping the confusing 'brace to the left' case

extensive API design negotiation: RegexpGroup/RegexpSearch/RegexpData naming, submatch function shape, start>end semantics rejected as 'too smart', ReplaceAll replaces ReplaceRegex, commit-organization expectations for large PRs

terminal-dependent Backspace vs Backspace2 encoding for Ctrl-Backspace; zyedidia: OldBackspace binding is the (confusingly undocumented) fix, terminals rarely differ Backspace/Backspace2 so micro treats them as equivalents by default; repeated newcomer requests through 2026 to document OldBackspace in keybindings.md, never actioned

PR #3335 (merged): unifies CopyLine/CutLine/DeleteLine/DuplicateLine to respect multi-line selections (previously only acted on the cursor's current line) and adds a new Duplicate action for selection-only duplication; default keybindings changed to action|actionLine pairs (e.g. Ctrl-c: Copy|CopyLine) to preserve old defaults. Discussion also revisits CutLine's append-to-clipboard (freshClip) behavior: the buggy, never-working lastCutTime 10-second reset is removed, and after debating renames (ClipLine, CutLineAppend, CutAndClipLine) the maintainers keep CutLine's existing append semantics as-is rather than splitting into a separate action, just documenting it and pointing users to CopyLine,DeleteLine for the non-appending alternative.
screen/tmux TERM lacks Shift-Arrow escape sequences in terminfo; owner's fix is mkinfo or TERM=xterm-256color, or raw bindings.json overrides — terminfo gap, not a tcell bug

zyedidia declines a dedicated vim/emacs mode but commits (2020-08-04) to upgrading the keybinding system for key-sequences (Ctrl-x Ctrl-f style) on the keybindings branch, prioritized so vim/emacs bindings could later ship as plugins; PR #1299 prototyped multi-key JSON bindings; still unmerged/open as of 2025 with a community vi-mode Lua plugin attempt (micro-vi-plugin) instead

tree-sitter integration proposal rejected for cgo dependency breaking cross-compilation (zyedidia); deferred to a possible future release rather than 2.0; recurring pure-Go preference from community; later WASM-compiled-grammar alternative floated (bartekpacia) with performance skepticism (anonyco), unresolved

Issue #3571 (open, long-running since 2024-12): pasting on Windows Terminal causes cascading auto-indent ('staircase' effect) because Windows Terminal intercepts Ctrl-v itself and forwards pasted text to micro as individual key events rather than as a bracketed paste (EventPaste), so autoindent applies per character as if typed. Root cause (confirmed 2026-01 by JoeKar via raw-input tracing and comparing against Microsoft's edit and Windows Terminal source) is that micro/tcell's legacy Windows console backend never requests ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT, so Windows Terminal never emits bracketed-paste sequences to it. Workarounds in the thread: rebind Paste to a non-intercepted key (e.g. Alt-v), or wrap Ctrl-v as 'setlocal autoindent off,Paste,setlocal autoindent on'. Confirmed fixed 2026-06/07 on the tcell/v3 branch, which does negotiate bracketed paste on Windows (verified working by both JoeKar and the reporter, with a noted redraw glitch on paste-over-selection and a status-bar PASTE indicator side effect).

new truecolor option (auto/on/off) replaces MICRO_TRUECOLOR env var; key finding: tcell already autodetects truecolor by default and micro was deliberately overriding it off, so the PR mostly exposes existing tcell behavior rather than adding new capability; default kept off initially for compat, later changed to auto (breaking change accepted after ~2 years of discussion); colorscheme tc/16-suffix naming inconsistencies noted as a follow-on problem

C++14/C23 digit-separator (') literal highlighting fix: applied to cpp.yaml only (not c.yaml, performance tradeoff decided by dmaluka), workaround error regex pending #3127 syntax-region rewrite (TODO to revert), later caused a regression (enum-value digits highlighted as numbers) fixed by follow-on PRs #3870/#3891/#3905

fixes #4050: concurrent sudo dd processes (truncate+write) raced on TCGETS2/TCSETS2, breaking sudo-rs; dmaluka traces the truncate-via-separate-dd design back to PR #3814/#3807 (need backup before truncate for safe sudo writes) and the eventual fix reorders safeWrite() to backup before openFile() for the sudo path (JoeKar's patch, adopted), returning OverwriteError on open failure; separately, the custom TTY pristine-state capture/restore around TempStart() overlaps tcell's own Init()/Fini() capture -- dmaluka suggests backporting tcell's Suspend()/Resume() instead but this PR keeps the local capture/restore; maintainers require commits split/squashed per their history preference; merged 2026-04-02 with a follow-up LookPath(sucmd) check to avoid spurious backups when sudo itself is missing

PR #2985 added +/- relative line prefixes to 'goto', breaking the existing nano-style 'goto -N' (from end of file, #1691); resolved with '~' reserved for from-end jumps and +/- for relative, merged 2023-11, but reverted 2024-03-17 by dmaluka after zoomosis reported the #1691 regression — reopened #2897 for community discussion of a separate relativegoto/jump command instead

softwrap origin: zyedidia confirmed as planned (2016-04), then shipped as `set softwrap on` (2016-10); later a toggle command/keybinding was added in v2.0.15 via #3783 (toggle softwrap), enabling e.g. Alt-Z like VS Code

Issue #4041 (open): pushback against PR #3618's removal of plugin settings.json writes, from a user whose plugins (chromakeys, miscutils) relied on SetGlobalOption persisting. Long, heated debate over whether write-protection should be unconditional or configurable, whether micro's JSON5 support is 'real' if writes discard comments/formatting, and alternatives (separate plugin-owned config files, an in-place JSON patcher, a SetGlobalOptionAndSave action, a whitelist of trusted plugins). Maintainers (dmaluka, JoeKar, Neko-Box-Coder) converge on a single extensible string-valued option `writesettings` (comma-separated keywords, e.g. `set`, `plugins`) controlling which write paths (the `set`/`bind` commands vs. plugin calls) persist to settings.json/bindings.json, defaulting to `set` only (today's post-#3618 behavior: plugins never write) — rejecting a per-plugin whitelist and a combined set+plugins boolean as over-engineering. Landed via #4046 and #4055 (both close this issue).

migrated nightly builds from zyedidia's manual/local process to GitHub Actions (cross-compile.sh rewritten with per-platform artifact helper, sha256 checksums, softprops/action-gh-release); needed GITHUB_TOKEN read/write workflow permissions (default changed Feb 2023), zyedidia disabled the old CI after confirming; follow-up PR #3418 fixed nightly asset naming so updates don't just accumulate old version-named files

zyedidia (2020): avoid Ubuntu's apt package, it was compiled in debug mode (spurious log files) and lags; prefer Debian's own repo (buster-backports era, up-to-date) or the released deb/getmic.ro installer; Calinou notes distro repos freeze at release so apt users don't get new micro versions until the next OS release

early (2016) design origin of bindings.json: zyedidia adopted pscollins's suggestion for a JSON keybinding config instead of hardcoding Mac Cmd shortcuts (rejected per #19, Ctrl used instead); some requested bindings (Ctrl-Backspace/Delete, Alt-Delete) are impossible because terminals never send them as distinct key events

new CursorToView{Top,Center,Bottom} actions to reposition cursor within the current view without scrolling; design settled through iteration: must account for soft-wrapped lines (SLoc not just line number) when checking if cursor is in view, scrollmargin is suppressed at buffer start/end to avoid unexpected jumps (deliberate, not a bug), multicursor state must be cleared via Buf.ClearCursors() before the move (RemoveAllMultiCursors() reorders badly since it itself calls Relocate()); explicitly NOT meant to fix PageUp/PageDown's cursor-jumps-to-top behavior — that's deferred to a separate action/behavior-change discussion (nano-style paging, referencing #1808) so as not to break existing user expectations by changing CursorPageUp/Down semantics directly

PR generalizes save-before-close prompt (open/term/quit) into closePrompt, and adds Buffer.Shared() to skip the prompt when another buffer already has the file open (matches #3559 for quit); review exposed that onSave/onSaveAs/preSave firing rules are undocumented and inconsistent across Save/SaveAs/quit-prompt paths (also seen in #3550, #3689) — maintainers decided documenting the mess is more realistic than unifying it

comment.lua commenttype override was clobbered on filetype change; fix (JoeKar) introduces comment.type via RegisterCommonOption plus DoSetOptionNative -- the key distinction dmaluka documents is that SetOptionNative marks an option as locally-overridden (survives reload/filetype change) while DoSetOptionNative just sets the buffer value without that mark, so per-filetype computed defaults must use DoSetOptionNative or they freeze at first value; commenttype renamed to comment.type with backward-compat alias kept permanently (dmaluka: no noisy runtime warning, just a doc note it may be deprecated later); recurring maintainer ask for one-functional-change-per-commit history for bisectability

PR #2810 (merged): fixes 13 separate syntax-highlighting bugs (bash, PHP, JS, Ruby, C/C++, etc.) whose root cause was the highlighter incorrectly gating regex matches containing literal ^ or $ characters behind a canMatchStart/canMatchEnd flag pair meant to represent line-start/line-end anchors -- but Go regexp/RE2 treats ^ and $ inside a pattern as matching every line-tokenized chunk passed to it (not just the true first/last line), so the gating silently dropped valid rule matches on later lines. JoeKar traced this via debug logging and screenshot comparisons against Vim/Emacs/Neovim, and the fix removes the start/end tracking entirely rather than trying to special-case it. zyedidia (owner) accepted the tradeoff of "compromising some incremental highlight performance" since most files are not huge, and noted the syntax highlighting system needs a full rework (linking the stalled github.com/zyedidia/flare project) that only lacked time/language files -- a separate, earlier rework attempt than the one tracked in [[highlighter-performance]].
